llm.summary: This skill does what it says, but it can perform live batch Consul deregistration and forward ACL tokens over unvalidated HTTP targets without strong confirmation or scoping.

dimensions.detail: The script sends PUT requests to user-supplied Consul agent URLs, runs requests in parallel by default, auto-converts bare hosts to plaintext HTTP, and does not validate destination hosts before sending requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence installer or dependency setup was found; the package contains a markdown skill file and one executable Python script, though usage examples hard-code a local absolute path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger includes the broad term "offline", examples instruct the AI to execute live deregistration, dry-run is optional rather than default, and there is no explicit confirmation step before destructive batch operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cross-session persistence or privilege escalation was found, but optional ACL token handling is sensitive because the token is accepted on the command line and attached to every selected destination.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose and bundled script align: deregister Consul service instances by service ID, agent list, agent file, or parsed curl commands.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only with trusted Consul agent addresses, prefer HTTPS, avoid passing ACL tokens on the command line, use narrowly scoped tokens, and require an explicit dry-run and human confirmation before any live batch deregistration.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network calls and script execution are expected for a Consul deregistration tool, but the artifact does not add clear tool limits or a required confirmation gate for live operations.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The "offline" trigger is broader than the deregistration purpose and could invoke the skill during unrelated operational discussion.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The skill documents dry-run support but does not prominently frame live deregistration as a destructive production-impacting action or make preview/confirmation the default path.
[T09] unexpected: ACL token authentication is purpose-aligned, but forwarding one supplied token to arbitrary user-provided destinations over default plaintext HTTP is not proportionate to safe credential handling.
